newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods narrowly mixed after new data.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods narrowly mixed after new data.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices were narrowly mixed midday Wednesday tracking firmer NYMEX and steady-to-weaker differentials, players said, after new EIA and API data showing sizeable draws on gasoline and distillate stocks last week.
Low demand for refined products and a surplus of "M4" winter-grade gasoline in New York Harbor loomed as bearish factors offsetting the otherwise bullish inventory data.

Indeed, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday unusually warm weather had reduced demand for refined products by 1.5 percent in February compared with the same month last year -- with deliveries of heating oil and diesel falling 5.4 percent to 3.52 million barrels.

Although gasoline demand last month was running about 0.3 percent higher than February, 1996, the API said total U.S. stocks last month were 5.4 percent lower than last year -- "the lowest for that time of year in several decades."
Nevertheless, differentials on New York Harbor "M4" were holding at an anemic 5.0 cents below the April print after easing a full cent Tuesday.
